headline: The Huang relief rally fully unwinds: chips and miners lead the selling, while oil names and the Dow's value stocks hold up into Wednesday's data pile-up

findings.headline: Data-centre spending doubts are back, and they have spread to metals
findings.body: Monday's euphoria over Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO lasted a day: Nvidia closed 5.9% lower as worries about whether AI data-centre spending will earn its keep returned, and the S&P 500 posted its eighth loss in nine sessions. The same unwind hit the copper and silver complex hard into the close, and First Quantum had a stock-specific blow on top after reporting a contractor fatality at Kansanshi in Zambia. Lundin Mining, Antofagasta and Anglo American were among the heaviest lagging names in our coverage, so the metals sell-off is now about AI demand sentiment as much as tariffs.

findings.headline: Energy led as Hormuz attacks continued, and Tullow clears its Ghana overhang
findings.body: Crude bounced off its lowest levels since August after Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted a container ship near Hormuz, following Monday's strikes on three vessels, so US oil majors were among the few leaders on the day. Separately, Tullow agreed a payment deal with Ghana worth up to $537.5m to settle its two tax arbitrations (about $387m plus penalties); it still needs Ghana's parliament to approve it, and Tullow says that unlocks its refinancing. That approval and the refinancing terms are the next catalysts, and the shares are still less than half their pre-ruling level in September.

findings.headline: Wednesday packs GDP, PCE, durables and claims into one 14:30 slot before Thanksgiving
findings.body: The Q3 GDP second estimate, October PCE inflation with income and spending, durable goods orders and weekly jobless claims all land at 14:30 Zurich, with new home sales at 16:00. With a December hike already close to fully priced after the AI rally stoked inflation worries, a hot core PCE matters more than a soft one because it would open the door to a bigger move. Thin pre-holiday liquidity can exaggerate the reaction.

sources.label: Schwab Network: Week ahead, GDP growth and earnings into Thanksgiving

view: Our view: This is still a rotation inside risk, out of AI chips and metals and into oil and value, rather than a broad flight to safety. The PCE print decides whether the rotation turns into wider de-risking: a hot core reading is the bigger risk for the miners and chips already lagging.
